guard: the delegation bound tests each part of a grant against the spawner's issued evidence at the spawner's own coordinate, refuses what it does not cover, and applies the token rule the ledger uses
why: A spawner may hand a helper any part of what it holds and never more. On a static mesh the
only record of what it holds is its issued evidence, which names subjects under its own
principal, so the grant is projected at the spawner's coordinate and the empty grant's rows
B1 drops the subtraction, so the coordinate's own rows decide and every grant refuses. B2
stops folding subscribe into the read ACL, so a subscribe-only grant escapes the bound. B3
stops testing publish rows. B4 forgets that run carries spawn. B5 mints a class rail for an
instance pin. B6 reads role:<r> as an ordinary token, so a held role cannot be handed on.

mutations.name: B1 test every projected row, not only the rows the field adds
mutations.expectRed: a grant inside the spawner's channels is within

mutations.name: B2 bound only the explicit read ACL
mutations.find: for (const ch of resolveReadAcl([...(grant.subscribe ?? [])], grant.allowSubscribe ? [...grant.allowSubscribe] : undefined))
mutations.expectRed: a subscribe-only grant is folded into the read ACL and bounded

mutations.name: B3 skip the publish test
mutations.expectRed: posting where the spawner may only read is named

mutations.name: B4 drop run-implies-spawn from the token rule
B5 mint a class rail beside an instance pin
mutations.find: : { endpoint: g.endpoint, command, instanceId: g.instanceId, instanceOnly: true }));
mutations.expectRed: the spawner's own instance pin is within

mutations.name: B6 read role:<r> as an ordinary capability token
mutations.replace: const role = undefined as string | undefined;
mutations.expectRed: role:<r> as a capability token is held when the spawner holds that role
